records_affected: Table rows 20 and 33; Zanthoxylum oxyphyllum Edgew.
observation: Same scientific binomial appears twice with vernacular names Prothoma and Mejenga and different RFC/UV values.
what_is_confirmed: Kew POWO accepts Zanthoxylum oxyphyllum Edgew. as a species; the paper presents two distinct vernacular-name observations and different quantitative values.
what_is_not_confirmed: It is not established whether the duplicate is a table error, separate local-name responses for one taxon, or different records aggregated under one botanical name. It does not establish two species.
recommended_treatment: Retain both source rows as observations; count one accepted binomial for species richness unless author/herbarium clarification supports a different treatment. Do not average RFC/UV or combine vernacular names.
follow_up: Check original PDF table and request clarification from author; compare submitted herbarium sheets and village-level informant data if accessible.

observation: Article abstract reports 48 species, while two rows carry the same scientific binomial.
what_is_confirmed: The article reports 48 ethnobotanical plant species and lists 48 table entries; a repeated binomial is present in two rows.
what_is_not_confirmed: The accessible evidence does not show whether the authors counted 48 unique accepted taxa or 48 records before resolving duplicate names.
recommended_treatment: Report as 48 source entries / author-reported species count; do not assert 48 taxonomically unique accepted species until all rows are reconciled.
follow_up: Reconcile every Majuli name against WFO/POWO and check herbarium vouchers; inspect the full table for other duplicate or outdated names.

observation: Name-level overlap does not guarantee same specimen identity, part used, or starter-culture role.
what_is_confirmed: Some scientific names match directly and one likely synonym match is documented in Kew.
what_is_not_confirmed: Full voucher-by-voucher comparison and consistent accepted-name normalization have not been completed.
recommended_treatment: Keep direct name matches, synonym matches, unresolved candidates, and non-matches as separate categories; never infer true absence from an accessible-text non-match.
follow_up: Extract full plant tables, accepted names, voucher identifiers, local names, plant parts, and village-level use from both studies.

records_affected: Hydrocotyle sibthorpioides; Vitex negundo; Scoparia dulcis
observation: The two studies report different family names for three directly matching binomials.
what_is_confirmed: POWO places Hydrocotyle sibthorpioides in Araliaceae, Vitex negundo in Lamiaceae, and Scoparia dulcis in Plantaginaceae; these match Majuli labels and differ from Sivasagar table labels.
what_is_not_confirmed: This audit does not determine whether source family labels reflect historical classification, source error, or an alternative taxonomic treatment; nor does name matching verify collected specimens.
recommended_treatment: Preserve source-published names and families in transcription tables; store POWO accepted name/family in a separate reconciliation layer and mark source-family conflicts explicitly.
follow_up: Complete POWO lookup for all 79 source rows; retain authority URL and lookup status for each row; voucher identity requires separate evidence.
